notes.title: Update Inbound
notes.content:
[p]For three hundred days, Jax Calder endured the hellscape of Bromius III, a wet barren rock scoured by wind and acid rain, where rusted metal groaned like ghosts and the sky never broke from its ashen shroud. Alone among the skeletons of the mining colony, he survived on emergency rations and grim determination, his only companion a failing environmental suit and the dim hum of a battered terminal he’d dragged into shelter piece by piece. Day after day, he worked—rebuilding the antenna from scrap, coding blind into cracked screens, shielding circuits with his body during electrical storms—until his hands bled and his breath stank of recycled air. 

Sleep came in fits but he was trained for this. And on the three-hundredth day, the terminal lit green. A signal broke through. And just before the storm season returned, a dark shape pierced the clouds—sleek, and familiar.  Just in time for Summer on Earth..
--
What some of you might remember is that AO was originally a game called [url="https://www.indiedb.com/games/zoo-base/news/aiming-for-misadventure-the-story-behind-zoo-base"]Zoo Base[/url]. And that Zoo Base was inspired by Star Zoo by Bay12. Fun fact - it wasn’t just inspired by it but we even got permission to directly call it a spiritual sequel.[/p][p]
Then everything got entirely too overthought. In an attempt to distinguish AO from predecessor Zoo Base. In hindsight that was a bad idea.[/p][p]
Which is not to say that I regret doing that. It’s just that with the state of the industry being what it is, there is a new kind of clarity hitting a lot of folks who have been indie for far longer than expected.[/p][p]
I think a lot of us are coming back to thinking about what fun is. Since like the tech industry as a whole there was a lot of problem solving of things that didn’t really need fixing. A lot of reintroductions to the wheel. And while the results are still valuable, I think a lot of engineers are figuring out how to apply those lessons and new technologies in a way that isn’t so heavily R&D.
[/p][p]Right now the server is (still) down in preparation for V7 - expected before July - which should put AO on a clear track to be exiting early access within a few subsequent patches. The game itself is being simplified because it actually outgrew itself around the time of the Linux announcement.  Which itself was marred with issues and quietly delayed and unknown outside of Discord.

More on all that in the next one! 

[/p]

notes.title: Apsis Online NPC Story Engine Update
notes.content:
The shanty-town outside the walls of Bromius Central at night is awash in shadows against firelit panels of rusted sheet metal.  Old hull parts dot the overgrowth and makeshift awnings while several human children in ragged tunics gather around a large murky puddle. All laughing and splashing beneath bare feet. A two-headed human brushes against your right shoulder with a glare from the face close enough to make out. His bluish bloated lips scowling with stringy chin-length dark hair flipped aside revealing scars along his cheek.  

The other head droops, remaining flailing helplessly at his side as he hurries away toward the city gate. Carrying a large metal container on his back secured by worn leather straps. Moon and firelight unsteadily reveal the faded letters “HGEC” as you determine that he may have been in the parts and organ trade. Here in the clone camps you can’t be too sure anyway. This is where anyone can end up after all. One way or another.

–
In the upcoming Apsis Online v7 I will be introducing a new simulation engine. Which is meant to activate the living game world starting with its first inhabitants (human or otherwise) and continuing through to their descendants and the resulting economic conditions that will effect the initial colony in more visible and impactful ways.

[img]https://cdn.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/steam/apps/1552260/ss_ce4ed6b05c435c7d173448da0535addb189b2f54.600x338.jpg?t=1696530880[/img]

Each NPC will also have their own story generated for them and at some point I will be making those accessible via their communications screen. This could be helpful in determining their underlying motives and potential skills. As well as compatibility with other NPC you may need to bring them around. A retired UESA soldier who is now a clone might not enjoy being asked to work with a Mutroon or Vane raider for example. Think [i]Football Manager[/i] in space.

This means that the player (you) will no longer be limited to small interactions with preset NPCs. The goal is to make you feel like an inhabitant of an existing place that you can impact with you decisions.  If you are familiar with the current NPC system you may have noticed a lot of speech options. The initial purpose of this was to test out their dynamic outlook on static game worlds down to things like recognizing the player, their faction and to some extent the choices they’ve already made.

Scaling this system means making the world feel very persistent. Which when coupled with more activities and embark options will allow anyone to effect everyone. Current plans include land and orbital patrols coupled with special tasks issued by NPCs. A lot like how adventure mode in DF Classic operates when looking for things to do.

So the overworld is returning as a real-time map allowing you to get information of zones as well as take specific actions in them for reasons that will also see expansions over the next few builds. NPCs will now settle scouted areas and can be raided. Players interrupting herds will effect the local economy. Air and land patrols will earn you experience and clout with the UESA which can unlock governance options when promoted. And dying may see you cloned and respawned in a clone camp where players can buy and sell grey market items like body parts, animals/people or simply hire personnel.

I may be jumping the gun on this post as we are still at least days away from a release but I felt it was important to do a little tell. In other news we’re still running on old servers but some optimization has made this bearable enough. A new server does exists but I'd hate to migrate then migrate back. The next patch will also include general stability and “quality of life” updates. More info coming soon. And thanks for your patience!

notes.title: Apsis Online
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39863067/aed5a407aa7c8ead0f0aad8d05ce561445758b98.gif[/img]

Apsis Online has been developed and distributed as freeware for years. Initially released as a custom-built singleplayer traditional roguelike game called [url=https://roguebasin.com/index.php/First_Paradise]First Paradise[/url] into what we have taken to calling a "multi-user roguelike". And while the game is currently playable with interactable NPCs, very minor exploration and combat. It is also the catalyst for a much richer experience to come. 

[b]So What's Next?[/b]

Well, at the moment there is only one planet and your own ship to explore.  Not just due to the limitations imposed by the current (and very soon, previous) hosting situation. But also because we have all seen how shallow procedurally generated worlds can be when left up to [i]the algorithm[/i] alone. I want to avoid this issue and besides, I have been feeling extra inspired by the stacks of science-fiction novels that make up the walls of my apartment.

So while there will soon be a proliferation of things to do on Bromius II, and the ship, there's also the matter of giving the simulation engine more to chew on. Even if limited in scope for now. The ultimate goal here is to present to the player this game world, however large, as affected by everyone else at all times. Both visually and in the form of a story that can be accessed both in-game and on the web. 

Now about the details.

[u]On Buildings[/u]

The plan for buildings is to create and/or gradually reactivate the various planetside facilities that will become useful to players who:

- Want to play and progress in the game without doing much combat. i.e via socially or PvE. This will actually extend into land and business ownership alongside construction features which have been teased in various capacities as far back as 2019. Except this time I will be looking at a more MUD-oriented experience in which persistent NPCs can generate logs that serve to advance their own personal story.

Each of these stories will be archived and viewable in-game and via a web browser. Your player also has a web page, generated at signup, with an event log and other information. This can be found via [u]apsisonline.vineyard.haus/YOURPLAYERNAME[/u] (in all caps). Although like most features the player log is currently temporarily dormant. 

- Want to feel like seemingly small decisions have an impact on the trajectory of the game world as a whole. I'm not talking about just some market prices either. Although attacking a herd of Mutroon will soon effect not just The Migration but the attitude of the Vane toward colonists and then, well. It's up to them. But it's really up to you too. 

This type of cause and effect will also apply to settlement governance. You will be able to lose your ship in a bet. Or an arm. Those at some point will be used to create npcs if that's all you've got to work with..see [url=https://apsisonline.vineyard.haus/handbook.pdf]the (outdated) handbook[/url]. This is all a simplification of a much deeper system and deserves its own post really. 

[u]Ground Combat and Expeditions (embarking)[/u]

- Ground combat has been completely redone and will soon vary more in terms of abilities and weapons available. Of course faction association and the skill orientation of the player will also play a part. Right now you can't choose where you go when you embark. This is due to not just the lack of groups/parties but ASCII art for big new bosses. However, the brand new controls, side view perspective and broader mechanics for not just those encounters but the rewards they give are almost entirely there. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39863067/3e31c7fbd67fd94c1d65f3579845172544ccc173.gif[/img]

So soon you can expect to be able to gather resources, chop down tress mine and fish.  Or declare your own settlement on the same planet. There will be weather and ACII art "cutscenes". A larger variety of environments with cool little ASCII art animations like bubbling lava, waterfalls, backgrounds and more. 

[u]Space Combat[/u]

- Space combat will inherit the visual properties of what was the old expedition/embark mode. Allowing for arrow key ship control within a system with the possibility of random encounters like boarding, abductions and more. Space is a big place!

[u]Built in Social Improvements and Many More Items[/u]

- This project has an entire [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bulletin_board_system]BBS[/url] embedded within it complete with a marketplace for players to swap items.  Unfortunately we need a lot more items!

- Chat channels are currently disabled but will return with public and private options as we migrate to better, faster servers in the very near future.


In short, there's a lot to do but so much done that both can and can't be seen. And so much more to say but it's 2am again. This is usually also the part where I drop the Trello but it's being re-organized and will be made available ASAP. So that new players can join in on the feedback loop. 

Looking forward to this next phase of the journey. Upward and onwards!

notes.title: Apsis Online V7 Update+
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39863067/b54ca1c06ac91367beca83592168a547c941d172.gif[/img]

Today is Waveday on the 15th of Rimmoon. The air is heavy with humidity.  I can feel the ground beneath as lush and damp as always.  Everywhere, the sound of water trickling and cascading is ever-present. Lightning illuminated a sheet of dark clouds pulled across the sky and, at times, this planet would be caught in a seemingly eternal rainfall.

The rain would become puddles and lakes but that is when you can see the Nutroon (`n) eggs float up toward the surface, waiting to hatch..

***

It is these creatures that will be the focus of V7 . As well as their less benign counterparts the Mutroon (`m). This update will coincide with a Steam launch. 

Today I was able to talk to our server sponsor to get test builds live again. So that means the most current build of the game is already up for internal testing.

Some other changes to expect by V7:

[+] Factions V1 will allow players to issue referrals to friends for mutual perks.
[+] Combat V2 is nothing at all like combat V1 and a departure from the traditional roguelike formula.
[+] Real-time data.
[+] Expanded NPC AI
[+] Expanded player profiles + player stories (auto-updated web pages).
[+] Bases (special points of interest on a planet, allows missions)
[+] Exploration V1

[b]Delayed features[/b]

Genetic engineering (I know)

For more upcoming information check out the Discord: https://discord.gg/m8KCv4j

notes.title: A Multi-User Roguelike
notes.content:
Since writing my first program in 2008 I had always been fascinated by digital communities. Experiments with Multi-User Dungeons like [url=https://www.play.net/gs4/]Gemstone 4[/url] had exposed me to an entire group of folks who could still vibe when less is more. Massive worlds imagined, a shared experience catalyzed in the visualization of text.

In the spirit of Bulletin Board Systems (BBS’), Reddit and Twitter I originally sought out to create a social network for minimalists. This ended up serving as a test-bed for so many more ideas though! With less overhead I was a able to turn experiments into new features and put all of it on top of an old game I had written. And that became something else entirely.

[b]The Story[/b]

Weak governments and social upheaval has ushered in an age of dystopianism. A world in which monopolistic corporations make the rules. Having normalized space travel with advancements in genetic engineering and propulsion, humanity set out to champion the frontier in hopes of discovering a new purpose.

[b]The Game[/b]

Apsis Online is a minimalist multi-user roguelike (MUR) based on the [url=http://www.roguebasin.com/index.php?title=First_Paradise]First Paradise[/url] project. The game is still early in development but is presented as a series of both multiplayer and single-player “sequences” set in a dark science­-fiction universe.

[center][img]https://miro.medium.com/max/1200/1*cxHMuMp3ue-yVVL3FR_Ziw.png[/img][/center]

[b]You are a voyager[/b]. A human, mentally and physically augmented for a new life in deep space. Your mission is to carve out a place for humanity among the stars. A largely hostile environment. Build outposts with resources found at the farthest reaches of the frontier itself. Survive, create new economies from scratch, capitalize and recruit others to join you.

[b]Platform & Aesthetics[/b]

Borrowing its likeness from the classic depiction of a player-character dating back to the original [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1443430/Rogue/]Rogue[/url]. RogueSpace is a game engine and social network. Built for speed and security by geeks for geeks who have a love for the command-line. Rendered in a sharp colorful ASCII style for the purist in all of us. Join the conversation!

[center][img]https://miro.medium.com/max/1200/1*7rsUgwLChW8cTZtFO-9_Lg.gif[/img][/center]

[list]
[*] Post, comment or subscribe to things you find most interesting.
[*] Create a page. Invite others, share privately or with the world.
[*] Join a Frontier Company, employ others and build an empire!
[*] Toggle in and out of gameplay sessions with ease.
[*] Email registration optional.
[/list]

This service will never store sensitive user data or any information about your machine or location.

[b]Worldbuilding & Economics[/b]

What is a good multiplayer game without a solid foundation in the form of game lore and player-driven stories? Apsis Online is built as a roguelike with procedurally generated events, planets and even perma-death. But don’t worry! Your wealth will always be saved to your account not the character.

[center][img]https://miro.medium.com/max/1200/1*S-o8VPY9GpLZRpZIMlLujw.gif[/img][/center]

Inspired by the likes of [url=https://cataclysmdda.org/]Cataclysm: Dark Days Ahead[/url] and [url=http://www.bay12games.com/dwarves/]Dwarf Fortress[/url] but carrying with it the literary spirit of multi-user dungeons like [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GemStone_IV]Gemstone IV[/url]. For years the underlying goal has been to consistently flesh out the game’s backstory through a combination of contributing to a growing [url=http://www.roguebasin.com/index.php?title=First_Paradise]wiki[/url] and even [url=http://my.w.tt/GpvlsfDoQ3]writing short stories[/url].

[center][img]https://miro.medium.com/max/1200/1*TK-3t5ZGZS2qZgAoPSCiTQ.gif[/img][/center]

For a while there were micro-fiction contests submitted by users before the platform for hosting these shut down (RIP [url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160506165302/http://www.desura.com/games/first-paradise]Desura[/url]!). It was at this point that @Space was conceived. The hope is to continue expanding on the idea of both user and A.I-generated stories in order to build a more immersive experience (despite the graphics!).
